title: Editor: Inputting Chinese with Microsoft Pinyin in scripts attached to scene nodes triggers text_edit.cpp column calculation error
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: Godot v4.5.1.stable.steam (I have only tested this version) ### System information Godot v4.5.1.stable (f62fdbd) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9144) - AMD Ryzen 7 2700X Eight-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.89 GiB memory ### Issue description **Core Problem** When using the **Microsoft Pinyin** IME to input Chinese characters **into comments** within GDScript files in the Godot editor, it triggers internal text index errors (`p_column` out of bounds). The manifestation of this bug is linked to whether the script's attachment status has changed during the editor session. **Key Findings** * **Absolute Requirement**: The bug **only occurs with the Microsoft Pinyin IME**. Switching to any other Chinese IME (e.g., Sogou Pinyin) eliminates the problem entirely. * **Context**: The bug was specifically reproduced **when writing Chinese text inside comments** (not within code string literals or as identifiers). * **Reliable Trigger Condition**: The error can be **consistently reproduced** after the following sequence: 1. **Detach** a script from its node (Right-click the node -> “Detach Script”). 2. **Re-attach** the same script (or a new one) to any node. 3. Attempt to input Chinese characters **into a comment** in that script. * **Notable Observation**: Upon a fresh start of the project and editor, inputting Chinese into comments of **previously attached scripts might work initially**. However, once the “detach and re-attach” operation is performed, the bug is “activated” and will occur stably. * **Error Messages**: ``` ERROR: scene/gui/text_edit.cpp:6387 - Condition “p_column > text[p_line].length()” is true. Returning: 0 ERROR: scene/gui/text_edit.cpp:4970 - Index p_column = XX is out of bounds (text_line.size() + 1 = XX). ``` **Excluded Factors** The following have been tested and confirmed **irrelevant**: * Scene type (2D/3D) and node hierarchy (root/child). * Physics interpolation setting and physics engine backend (GodotPhysics/Jolt). * File encoding (confirmed UTF-8). * System clipboard state. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new project or open any existing project in Godot Editor (v4.5.1). 2. Ensure the **Microsoft Pinyin** IME is the active input method. 3. In the scene, **detach** a script from a node (right-click the node -> “Detach Script”), then **re-attach** the same (or a new) script. *(This is the key trigger)*. 4. Open the re-attached script file. 5. Place the cursor after a `#` symbol (to write a comment) and type any Chinese character. 6. The error will appear immediately in the Output panel. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
